lines: Old Fenwick: My boy went down the Shatterfloor for copper. The mine kept him and sent back his boots.
Old Fenwick: Good boots. Wipe your feet on the way out.
Tender Bea: Fen water, boiled twice. Once for the mud, once for the leeches.
Tender Bea: Sit. Your team can drink their fill.
Clerk Dirk: Towels, tonics, tide tables. The tables are free. They are also wrong.

Keeper Ilka: Brook water through a willow root. It tastes of bark and patience.
Clerk Maren: Ebbe keeps the cold stock outside. In here it is the same stock, only warmer.

lines: Widow Marit: My husband rowed the ferry for thirty years. One day the ferry came back and he did not.
Widow Marit: The company sent flowers. And the bill for the oar.
Nurse Trudi: The dye works took the colour from the river. The spring kept a little. Rest.
Dyer Konrad: Forty years I dyed cloth blue. Now my hands are blue and the cloth is grey.
Dyer Konrad: Fair trade, says the guild.
Shepherd Olm: The fog takes a sheep a week. I stopped naming them.
Shepherd Olm: Then I stopped counting them. Now I sleep fine.
Rift Watcher Ida: I watch the edge so you don't have to. Nobody pays me.
Rift Watcher Ida: Nobody needs to. The edge is very convincing.
